newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine courts indict banker in IBM bribe case.
newsitem.headline: Argentine courts indict banker in IBM bribe case.

text.p: An Argentina's federal court said late Tuesday it ordered the indictment of a banker in connection with a bribery scandal involving U.S. computer maker IBM.

The court indicted Carlos Alberto Rohm, vice-president of the Banco General de Negocios (BGN), for having allegedly "covered up" bribes allegedly paid in 1993 to ensure the local unit of IBM clinched a $250 million deal with Argentina's Banco Nacion.

Rohm "used the financial leverage derived from his position as managing director of BGN and of the Compania General de Negocios, based in Uruguay, to cover up the money that (IBM subcontractor) CCR had received illegally," the court said in a statement.
Twelve people have now been indicted in the case, including former Banco Nacion chairman Aldo Dadone and IBM Argentina's former president and vice-president, Ricardo Martorana and Gustavo Soriani.
IBM Argentina has denied any corruption, but admitted errors and actions "inconsistent with company policy."

Banco Nacion last year cancelled the deal to install a new computer system in its headquarters and 252 branches and sued IBM Argentina for $174 million. IBM has counter-sued for $86 million alleging breach of contract.
